question: During the Offset Back/Left exercise on the Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test, what must you do?
choice_a: Drive straight forward the outer boundary, then back the vehicle into the opposite lane until the front of your vehicle has passed the first set of cones without striking boundary lines or cones
choice_b: Back the vehicle into an alley, bringing the rear as close as possible to the rear of the alley
choice_c: Drive forward and stop with the front of the vehicle within a marked box without going past it
choice_d: Back straight through the alley until the front of the vehicle clears the last set of cones
explanation: The manual states you drive straight forward the outer boundary, then back into the opposite lane until the front of your vehicle passes the first set of cones without striking boundary lines or cones.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12 - Offset Back/Left exercise

question: In the Basic Control Skills Test scoring system, what is a 'pull-up'?
choice_a: Backing up on a forward-moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position
choice_b: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position; you are not penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number counts as errors
choice_c: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its external position while backing
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position, scored on Exercise 2 and Exercise 4; initial pull-ups are not penalized but excessive pull-ups count as errors.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Pull-ups

question: What is scored as a 'back-up' during the Basic Control Skills Test, and on which exercise?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment, scored on Exercise 2 and Exercise 4
choice_b: Stopping without changing direction, scored on Exercise 1
choice_c: Backing up on a forward-moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position, scored on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_d: Crossing a boundary line while exiting the vehicle, scored on Exercise 4
explanation: The manual defines a back-up as backing up on a forward-moving exercise to clear an encroachment or get a better position, scored specifically on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Back-ups

question: Does stopping without changing direction count as a pull-up during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Yes, it always counts as one pull-up
choice_b: Yes, but only if it happens more than once
choice_c: It counts as an encroachment instead
choice_d: No, stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up
explanation: The manual explicitly states that stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Pull-ups

question: What counts as an 'encroachment' on the Basic Control Skills Test?
choice_a: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors (or a unique vehicle part at or above door mirror height)
choice_b: Exiting the vehicle more than the allowed number of free looks
choice_c: Pulling forward to gain a better backing position
choice_d: Failing to sound the horn when an exercise is complete
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of the vehicle other than the mirrors (door or fender) or unique vehicle parts at door mirror height or higher.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Encroachments

question: If you encroach on an exercise boundary line or cone, what must you do?
choice_a: Continue the exercise and let the examiner note it silently
choice_b: Stop immediately when signaled by the examiner and return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries
choice_c: Automatically fail the Basic Control Skills Test
choice_d: Restart the exercise from the very beginning
explanation: The manual states that if you have encroached, the examiner will stop you and you must return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries, stopping immediately when signaled by the examiner.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Encroachments

question: Before exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise ('look'), what must you do?
choice_a: Sound the horn twice and turn off the engine
choice_b: Simply open the door and step out
choice_c: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral, then safely exit by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact
choice_d: Wait for the examiner to physically open the door for you
explanation: The manual requires that before exiting/entering the vehicle to check its position, you must set the parking brake(s), place the vehicle in neutral, and safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks

question: What may result if you open your vehicle door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park) during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: It counts only as a single 'look'
choice_b: It counts as one encroachment
choice_c: Nothing, as long as the door is closed quickly
choice_d: It may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act
explanation: The manual warns that if you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks/Unsafe Act

question: How many free looks are you allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: A maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 and two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_b: Two free looks on Exercise 2 and one free look on Exercise 4
choice_c: No free looks are allowed on either exercise
choice_d: Three free looks on each exercise
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, free look allowances

question: On which exercises are you scored for the final position of the vehicle?
choice_a: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_b: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_c: All four exercises equally
choice_d: Only Exercise 1 - Forward Stop
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Final Position

question: What can result from failing to follow the examiner's instructions for completing a Basic Control Skills exercise as directed?
choice_a: A minor point deduction with no other consequence
choice_b: A warning, with the exercise repeated at no penalty
choice_c: An automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner
choice_d: Only a requirement to redo that one exercise
explanation: The manual states that failure to follow examiner instructions for completing the exercise as directed may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times may you stop the vehicle while driving through the alley?
choice_a: Up to two times
choice_b: As many times as needed to align the front of the vehicle
choice_c: Three times
choice_d: Only once
explanation: The manual states you drive forward through the alley and stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box; you may stop only once.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.2.1 - Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: After completing Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, what must you do before the examiner scores the exercise?
choice_a: Set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn
choice_b: Immediately exit the vehicle to check the front position
choice_c: Activate your four-way emergency flashers
choice_d: Honk once and pull forward again
explanation: The manual states that when you have stopped, you must set your parking brake, shift to neutral, and sound the horn; the examiner will then score the exercise.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.2.1 - Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: On Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, how many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are you allowed?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and two exits
choice_b: One free pull-up and you may safely exit the vehicle only one time
choice_c: No free pull-ups but one free exit
choice_d: Unlimited free pull-ups but no exits allowed
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle during Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.2.2 - Exercise 2, Straight-Line Backing

question: During Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, are you allowed any free back-ups or permitted to exit the vehicle?
choice_a: One free back-up and one exit are allowed
choice_b: Two free back-ups are allowed, but no exits
choice_c: There are no free back-ups, and you are not permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise
choice_d: Unlimited back-ups are allowed, with one free exit
explanation: The manual states there are NO free back-ups on Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and you are NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.2.3 - Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, within how many feet of the rear of the alley must the rear-most part of your vehicle be brought?
choice_a: Ten feet
choice_b: Five feet
choice_c: One foot
choice_d: Three feet
explanation: The manual states you must offset back into the alley, bringing the rear most part of your vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups and vehicle exits are allowed during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and a maximum of two exits to check around the vehicle
choice_b: One free pull-up and one exit
choice_c: No free pull-ups but three exits
choice_d: Unlimited pull-ups and exits
explanation: The manual states you are allowed two free pull-ups and may exit the vehicle a maximum of two times to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 12M.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: According to the on-road driving turn procedures, when does 'unsafe coasting' occur?
choice_a: Whenever you shift gears while approaching a turn
choice_b: When your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in Neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
choice_c: When you brake smoothly before entering a turn
choice_d: When you activate your turn signal too early
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in Neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: What must you do with your hands and gears while actually making a turn during the road test?
choice_a: Change gears smoothly to maintain power through the turn
choice_b: Keep one hand on the wheel and one on the turn signal
choice_c: Keep both hands on the steering wheel and do not change gears during the turn
choice_d: Downshift halfway through the turn to control speed
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to keep both hands on the steering wheel during the turn and to not change gears during the turn.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: When approaching an intersection with a stop sign, signal, or stop line during the road test, what is required?
choice_a: A rolling stop is acceptable if no other traffic is present
choice_b: Stop only if pedestrians are visible in the crosswalk
choice_c: Maintain speed and yield only to crossing traffic
choice_d: Come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind the stop line, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle ahead, and the vehicle must not roll forward or backward
explanation: The manual requires coming to a complete stop (no coasting) behind stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines while maintaining a safe gap, and states the vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: During the Urban/Rural Straight portion of the road test, where should your vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: Centered in the proper (right-most) lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic without exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_b: In the left-most passing lane at all times
choice_c: Straddling the center line for maximum visibility
choice_d: In whichever lane currently has the least traffic
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.3 - Urban/Rural Straight

question: During the lane-change portion of the road test, what is the correct procedure?
choice_a: Change lanes immediately, then check traffic and signal afterward
choice_b: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so
choice_c: Signal only if another vehicle is nearby
choice_d: Change lanes to the left only; you will not be asked to return to the right
explanation: The manual states you should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so, and you will be asked to change left then back to the right.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.4 - Lane Changes

question: Once on the expressway exit ramp, what must you continue to do?
choice_a: Accelerate to merge back with mainline traffic before decelerating
choice_b: Change lanes freely to find the fastest exit path
choice_c: Continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles
choice_d: Come to a complete stop before entering the ramp
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.5 - Expressway

question: Once you have brought your vehicle to a stop during the Stop/Start maneuver, what must you do (in addition to being parallel to the curb or shoulder)?
choice_a: Immediately exit the vehicle to check its position
choice_b: Leave the vehicle in gear with your foot on the clutch
choice_c: Sound the horn to notify the examiner
choice_d: Cancel your turn signal, activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, move the gear shift to Neutral or Park, and remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals
explanation: The manual lists the once-stopped sequence as: vehicle parallel and out of traffic flow, not blocking anything, cancel turn signal, activate four-way flashers, apply parking brake, shift to Neutral or Park, and remove feet from the brake and clutch pedals.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve during the road test, what should you do before entering it?
choice_a: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_c: Shift gears while turning through the curve to keep power
choice_d: Brake continuously throughout the entire curve
explanation: The manual instructs that before entering the curve, you should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.7 - Curve

question: For a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards, within what distance must the vehicle stop from the nearest rail at a railroad crossing (unless the crossing is exempt)?
choice_a: Within 100 feet but not less than 50 feet
choice_b: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: Within 25 feet but not less than 10 feet
choice_d: Exactly at the crossing gate arm
explanation: The manual states the vehicle must stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: When should a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle driver activate and deactivate the four-way flashers at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Activate only after crossing, deactivate before the next intersection
choice_b: Activate and keep on continuously for the rest of the route
choice_c: Activate as the vehicle approaches the crossing, and deactivate after the vehicle crosses the tracks
choice_d: Flashers are not required at railroad crossings
explanation: The manual states that as the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, activate the four-way flashers, and that four-way flashers should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the road test, what might the examiner ask you to identify, as opposed to after crossing a bridge?
choice_a: The name of the road authority responsible for the overpass
choice_b: The speed limit posted on the overpass
choice_c: The posted weight limit (this is asked after crossing a bridge instead)
choice_d: The posted clearance or height
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass you may be asked what the posted clearance or height was, while after going over a bridge you may be asked what the posted weight limit was.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.9 - Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: For a school bus endorsement road test, how far away from students must the school bus come to a complete stop when discharging them?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away from the students at the stop
choice_b: At least 25 feet away
choice_c: At least 3 feet away
choice_d: There is no specified minimum distance
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for the student discharge, you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.10 - Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: According to the general driving behavior category for Brake Usage, what should you avoid doing?
choice_a: Using steady, smooth pressure on the brake
choice_b: Riding or pumping the brake; you should brake smoothly using steady pressure instead
choice_c: Braking before entering an intersection
choice_d: Checking your mirrors after braking
explanation: The manual's Brake Usage category states: do not ride or pump the brake, and do not brake harshly — brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Wyoming CDL Manual (Oct 2024), Section 13.1.11(c) - Brake Usage
